RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-06FC809FB2-91216
Member: Harper Grant, Member ID W271226534
Requested Service: Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-19
Treating Surgeon: Duval, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Aetna Appeals Review Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29914 (hip arthroscopy) issued on 2026-08-19, reference number POC-06FC809FB2-91216. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity."

This determination was made under Aetna's applicable medical policy for this procedure, Clinical Policy Bulletin Number 0736, "Hip Preservation Surgery," which explicitly lists CPT 29914 ("Arthroscopy, hip, surgical; with femoroplasty (ie, treatment of cam lesion)") among the codes subject to its medical necessity criteria. I am submitting this appeal along with the complete clinical record to demonstrate that the medical necessity criteria in CPB 0736 are met, and I am asking Aetna to identify, in writing, any specific element it still considers unaddressed so that it can be supplied promptly.

Below I map the clinical record already in the prior authorization packet to the medical necessity criteria set out in CPB 0736:

1. Diagnosis of FAI on imaging with labral pathology and cam/pincer/pistol-grip findings
CPB 0736 requires "[d]iagnosis of definite femoro-acetabular impingement (FAI) defined by appropriate imaging studies (X-rays, MRI or CT scans), showing labral pathology (e.g. partial or full thickness labral tearing or labral damage) with one or more of the following: cam impingement (alpha angle greater than 50 degrees) ... or pistol grip deformity (non-spherical femoral head shape)."
- MRI arthrogram of the hip dated 2026-07-17 documents an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement and an alpha angle of 68 degrees, which exceeds the 50-degree threshold stated in the policy. This finding is already in the submitted packet.

2. Moderate to severe symptoms typical of FAI for at least 6 months
CPB 0736 requires "[m]oderate to severe symptoms typical of FAI (hip or groin pain that is worsened by flexion activities (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) that significantly limits activities, with duration of at least 6 months."
- The record documents 12 months of progressive hip pain unrelieved by rest, with sharp anterior groin pain on sitting and pivoting, and inability to run or squat — symptom duration and character consistent with this criterion.

3. Positive impingement sign
CPB 0736 requires a "[p]ositive impingement sign with sudden pain on 90 degree hip flexion with adduction and internal rotation or extension and external rotation."
- The exam note documents "positive provocative testing on the affected side" with pain-limited range of motion. If the specific maneuver and positioning used (flexion/adduction/internal rotation, or extension/external rotation) is not already itemized in the exam note on file, we ask that this be treated as [confirmation/clarification of impingement testing technique] and, if needed, Dr. Duval will supplement the note to specify the exact positive maneuver performed.

4. Failure of conservative treatment
CPB 0736 requires "[f]ailure to respond to all available conservative treatment options including: activity modification (e.g., restriction of athletic pursuits and avoidance of symptomatic motion), pharmacological intervention (e.g., non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs [NSAIDS]), injections of local anesthetics into the joint) and physiotherapy. The treatment should be for at least 12 weeks in the past year with at least 6 weeks being formal physiotherapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist not virtual). Physical therapy (PT) needs to be confirmed either by the actual PT notes, or by documentation in the member claims history."
- The record documents 14 weeks of supervised, in-person physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification, from 2026-04-18 to 2026-07-25, with 16 visits completed and documented in the physical therapy discharge note. This exceeds both the 12-week overall conservative-care window and the 6-week formal in-person physiotherapy minimum in the policy.
- NSAIDs were used for 4 months with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection was administered on 2026-05-10, giving only 4 weeks of partial relief. We note the policy text refers to "injections of local anesthetics into the joint" as an example of pharmacologic/injection-based conservative treatment; the corticosteroid injection in this record was administered for symptom control and, together with the NSAID trial and formal physiotherapy, demonstrates that conservative measures have been attempted and have failed to provide durable relief. If Aetna requires documentation of an intra-articular local anesthetic injection specifically, please identify that requirement so it can be addressed with Dr. Duval.

5. Absence of advanced osteoarthritis / severe cartilage injury
CPB 0736 requires "[a]bsence of advanced osteoarthritis change on pre-operative X-ray (Tonnis grade 2 or more) or severe cartilage injury (Outerbridge grade III or IV)."
- The 2026-07-17 MRI arthrogram documents Tonnis grade 0, well below the grade-2-or-greater exclusion threshold in the policy.

6. Absence of joint space narrowing
CPB 0736 requires "[a]bsence of joint space narrowing on plain radiograph of the pelvis. Joint space is not less than 2 mm wide anywhere along the sourcil."
- The MRI arthrogram documents joint space preserved. If Aetna requires a plain pelvic radiograph specifically (as opposed to MRI) to confirm joint space width, please advise, and we will arrange for [plain radiograph of the pelvis] to be obtained and submitted.

7. Absence of generalized joint laxity/connective tissue disorder and osteogenesis imperfecta; all other sources of hip pain ruled out
CPB 0736 also requires that the "[m]ember does not have generalized joint laxity especially in diseases connected with hypermobility of the joints, such as Marfan syndrome and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome," that the "[m]ember does not have osteogenesis imperfecta," and that "[a]ll other potential sources of hip pain have been ruled out."
- The clinical summary provided does not document these items explicitly. We are prepared to have Dr. Duval submit a supplemental attestation addressing [absence of connective tissue/hypermobility disorder], [absence of osteogenesis imperfecta], and [differential diagnosis ruling out other sources of hip pain], and would appreciate confirmation that this is the specific gap Aetna is referring to as "incomplete" documentation, so that it can be corrected without further delay.

I want to be clear that beyond the language quoted directly above from CPB 0736, I have not been able to independently confirm from a publicly retrieved source the current effective or last-revised date of that bulletin, and I am not attributing any additional policy language to Aetna beyond what is quoted here. To the extent Aetna's determination relied on any other internal criterion, guideline, or version of the policy not reflected above, I request — consistent with the member's appeal rights — that Aetna identify that specific criterion and provide a copy of the exact policy language relied upon, so the record can be completed accordingly.

In summary, the submitted record shows: symptom duration of 12 months; a supervised, in-person physical therapy course of 14 weeks/16 visits (exceeding the policy's 12-week/6-week formal PT requirement); a 4-month NSAID trial; a corticosteroid injection with only transient benefit; MRI arthrogram evidence of an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type FAI and an alpha angle of 68 degrees; Tonnis grade 0; and preserved joint space. This documentation directly maps to the core medical necessity criteria in CPB 0736 for femoro-acetabular surgery and for hip arthroscopy to repair a labral tear as an adjunct to FAI surgery. I ask that Aetna reverse its denial and approve CPT 29914, or, if any specific item remains outstanding, identify it precisely so it can be supplied without delay.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the expected timeframe for a decision. I understand this appeal must be received within 180 days of the 2026-08-19 notice, i.e., by 2027-02-15, and this letter is being submitted well within that deadline.

Enclosed/attached with this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-18 to 2026-07-25, 16 visits)
- Medication and injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-05-10)
- MRI arthrogram report dated 2026-07-17
- Clinic examination notes documenting provocative testing and functional limitations
- [Any supplemental surgeon attestation addressing connective tissue disorder/osteogenesis imperfecta/differential diagnosis, if obtained]
- Copy of the original denial notice (reference POC-06FC809FB2-91216)
- [Signed Member Complaint and Appeal Form, if used]

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Harper Grant
